statusPolicy.pending: Not started or waiting for dependencies.
statusPolicy.in_progress: Actively being implemented. At most one implementation task should normally have this status.
statusPolicy.done: Acceptance criteria were verified and evidence is recorded.
statusPolicy.blocked: Cannot proceed without an external prerequisite; blockedReason must be present.

tasks.title: Define the product and technical architecture
acceptanceCriteria: The mobile gameplay, multiplayer authority, hosting, delivery, cost, security, testing, and rollout decisions are documented.
The document records the selected technology and deferred features.

tasks.title: Create the TypeScript monorepo workspace
acceptanceCriteria: npm workspaces include client, server, protocol, game-config, and simulation packages.
A locked dependency install succeeds.
Root scripts expose build, typecheck, lint, format check, and test commands.

tasks.title: Define shared linting, formatting, and TypeScript configuration
acceptanceCriteria: All workspaces use strict TypeScript.
ESLint and Prettier run from the repository root.
Generated build output is ignored.

tasks.title: Implement the versioned realtime protocol package
acceptanceCriteria: Client-to-server and server-to-client message schemas are runtime validated.
The handshake carries a protocol version.
Valid and invalid message tests pass.

tasks.title: Implement versioned game configuration
acceptanceCriteria: Match, movement, health, pistol, and network tuning values are typed and versioned.
Invalid configuration is rejected by tests.

tasks.title: Create the Babylon.js PWA shell
acceptanceCriteria: The client renders a Babylon.js scene.
The production build uses the GitHub Pages repository base path.
The web manifest and service worker make the shell installable.
Unsupported WebGL clients see an explicit compatibility message.

tasks.title: Create the Cloud Run server shell
acceptanceCriteria: The server exposes health, readiness, and version endpoints.
The server shuts down gracefully.
A production container builds and runs as a non-root user.
evidence: Docker image ran as user node and returned healthy endpoints (2026-09-19)

tasks.title: Add repository continuous integration
acceptanceCriteria: Pull requests run install, format, lint, typecheck, unit tests, production builds, container build, and browser smoke tests.
Workflow permissions default to read-only.
Build artifacts are retained for inspection.

tasks.title: Add GitHub Pages deployment
acceptanceCriteria: A successful main-branch workflow deploys the client through the github-pages environment.
The deployed URL passes a smoke test.
Only generated build output is uploaded.
evidence: GitHub Actions deployment and its public URL/manifest smoke test passed in run 35490328708 on 2026-09-20.

tasks.title: Document and perform initial Google Cloud setup
acceptanceCriteria: The setup record contains resource names and verification evidence without credentials.
Billing alerts are configured before public deployment.
Required APIs, Artifact Registry, service accounts, and the selected Central European region are recorded.
evidence: Created billed data project scooter-shooter-jr-2026 and runtime project scooter-shooter-run-2026 in europe-west3 under one EUR 20 budget with 50/75/90/100 percent alerts.

Created Artifact Registry, Firestore, Firebase web app, anonymous and Google sign-in providers, runtime and deployment service accounts, monitoring resources, and documented non-secret evidence in docs/operations/initial-cloud-setup.md.
externalPrerequisites: Permission to configure the GitHub repository

tasks.title: Configure keyless GitHub-to-Google deployment
acceptanceCriteria: Workload Identity Federation is restricted to this repository and production branch or environment.
No downloaded service-account key is stored in GitHub.
The deployment identity has only the required permissions.
evidence: Created projects/473376195766/locations/global/workloadIdentityPools/github-actions/providers/github with repository and refs/heads/main attribute restrictions.
Configured the production GitHub environment for main and stored only non-secret deployment/Firebase variables; verified both service accounts have no user-managed keys.
The keyless GitHub deployment authenticated, pushed an image, deployed a Cloud Run revision, and verified public endpoints in run 35493950607.

tasks.title: Add Cloud Run production deployment
acceptanceCriteria: Main deploys an immutable server image to Artifact Registry and Cloud Run.
The workflow sets explicit region, CPU, memory, concurrency, timeout, minimum zero instances, and maximum one instance.
Health and version checks verify the new revision.
evidence: GitHub run 35493950607 authenticated keylessly, pushed immutable image f78128305221c1553640da5421fbe1506076473d, and deployed a ready revision with explicit resource limits.
The deployment workflow verified /livez, /readyz, and /version with HTTP 200 against https://scooter-shooter-server-mpdmk2zohq-ey.a.run.app.

tasks.title: Establish cost and operations guardrails
acceptanceCriteria: Budget notification thresholds below EUR 20 are verified.
Artifact retention, log exclusions, uptime checks, and error alerts are recorded.
An emergency matchmaking shutdown procedure is documented.
evidence: A shared EUR 20 budget covers both data and runtime projects with 50/75/90/100 percent thresholds.
Configured a /livez uptime check, email-backed unavailability/error/instance alerts, high-volume log exclusions, and Artifact Registry cleanup retaining 10 recent images.
Tested the emergency ingress shutdown and added a monthly cost-review workflow; its first run created issue #1.

tasks.title: Create the Blocktown map blockout
acceptanceCriteria: The scene includes two protected spawns, a central plaza, flank routes, cover, and bounded play space.
The blockout uses mobile-appropriate geometry and materials.

tasks.title: Implement the local player character and collision
acceptanceCriteria: The player moves, strafes, rotates, collides with the world, and remains inside map bounds.
Movement parameters come from shared game configuration.

tasks.title: Implement the third-person camera
acceptanceCriteria: The camera follows over the shoulder with bounded pitch and configurable sensitivity.
Camera collision prevents wall clipping.

tasks.title: Implement the blue movement joystick
acceptanceCriteria: The joystick tracks its originating touch, applies a dead zone, clamps magnitude, and resets on release.
Movement is camera-relative.

tasks.title: Implement the red aim and fire joystick
acceptanceCriteria: The joystick controls yaw and pitch with its own tracked touch.
Crossing the configurable threshold emits fire intent and returning inside stops it.
evidence: npm run test:smoke (2 mobile Chromium tests, 2026-09-19)

tasks.title: Implement responsive orientation-aware HUD
acceptanceCriteria: Gameplay controls respect device safe areas in landscape.
Portrait menus work and gameplay displays a rotate-device interstitial.
Touch targets meet the 44 CSS-pixel baseline.
evidence: npm run test:smoke (3 mobile Chromium tests, 2026-09-19)

tasks.title: Add client performance instrumentation and reduced effects
acceptanceCriteria: Developers can inspect FPS, frame time, draw calls, and memory where supported.
Reduced-effects mode disables costly optional effects.
The vertical slice holds 30 FPS on the selected minimum test device.
evidence: npm run test:smoke (4 mobile Chromium tests, 2026-09-19)
tasks.blockedReason: Instrumentation and reduced-effects mode are implemented, but the 30 FPS acceptance gate requires selecting and testing a physical minimum mobile device.

tasks.title: Implement pistol configuration and presentation
acceptanceCriteria: The pistol displays muzzle flash, recoil, tracer, audio, ammo, and reload state.
Gameplay values are configuration-driven.
evidence: npm run test:smoke (automatic fire and ammo update, 2026-09-19)

tasks.title: Implement hitscan and hit geometry in the local harness
acceptanceCriteria: Shots stop at world geometry and only hit targets within range.
The local harness separates shot intent from authoritative resolution.
evidence: npm run test:smoke (shot resolution result asserted, 2026-09-19)

tasks.title: Implement health, damage, elimination, and respawn simulation
acceptanceCriteria: Health is bounded and damage cannot apply to eliminated players.
Elimination disables movement and firing.
Respawn restores configured state and supports temporary protection.

tasks.title: Implement Team Deathmatch rules
acceptanceCriteria: Waiting, countdown, in-progress, ended, and reset states are deterministic.
Score limit, timer, teams, draws, joins, leaves, and eliminations are covered by tests.
evidence: Implemented a deterministic TeamDeathmatch state machine covering balanced joins, safe leaves, countdown cancellation, timed and score-limit endings, draws, resets, and elimination scoring.
Validated 6 Team Deathmatch tests and all 11 simulation tests on 2026-04-10.

tasks.title: Complete the combat HUD and feedback
acceptanceCriteria: HUD shows health, ammunition, timer, score, crosshair, hit confirmation, elimination, respawn, and result states.
Team information uses labels or icons in addition to color.
evidence: Integrated the shared health, respawn, and Team Deathmatch simulations into the offline target harness.
HUD now renders labeled team scores, match countdown/timer/results, health, ammunition, hit/elimination feedback, and target respawn state.
Full npm run validate and all 4 Playwright mobile Chromium smoke tests passed on 2026-04-10.

tasks.title: Add configurable training bots
acceptanceCriteria: Players choose between one and eight bots before entering offline training.
Every selected bot spawns as an enemy, moves toward the player, attacks, takes damage, scores eliminations, and respawns.
Leaving and restarting training applies the newly selected bot count without retaining the previous scene.
evidence: apps/client/src/game/TrainingBotController.ts implements collision-aware chase/strafe movement, ranged attacks, and world-geometry line-of-sight checks.
OfflineCombatController manages independent bot and player health, eliminations, team scoring, spawn protection, and respawns.
The entry screen selects one through eight bots and Playwright verifies maximum selection plus scene teardown and restart with a changed count.
A deployed playtest exposed a missing Babylon collision coordinator import that froze bot movement and the match countdown; the runtime registration is now explicit.
Passive combat, movement/fire, and bot-count restart sessions passed locally after the fix; offline countdown was reduced to three seconds.
npm run validate and all 5 deeper mobile Chromium gameplay tests passed on 2026-09-20.

tasks.title: Implement fixed top-down controls and camera
acceptanceCriteria: The camera follows the player from a fixed elevated angle without player-controlled orbit or zoom.
Movement remains screen-relative while touch aiming independently controls player facing and firing.
Player and bot collision capsules stay grounded during movement.
evidence: TopDownCamera, AimController, LocalPlayerController, PistolController, and TrainingBotController implement fixed-camera world-space controls and grounded collision movement.
Playwright verifies top-down mode, independent touch movement and aiming, live grounded bot movement, firing, and runtime stability on 2026-09-20.

tasks.title: Add complete desktop gameplay controls
acceptanceCriteria: WASD and arrow keys move the player relative to the camera.
Mouse position controls world-space aim and holding the left button fires.
Desktop controls do not interfere with the mobile dual-stick controls.
evidence: DesktopAimController implements mouse-plane aiming and left-button fire while LocalPlayerController handles keyboard movement.
Dedicated desktop Chromium tests verify keyboard movement, mouse aim, and mouse fire while the mobile Chromium control tests continue to pass on 2026-09-20.

tasks.title: Integrate licensed low-poly game models
acceptanceCriteria: Player, bots, city buildings, props, and vehicles use redistributable low-poly models.
Every imported asset has recorded source and license provenance.
Model loading works from the GitHub Pages base path and remains within the PWA precache limit.
evidence: Selected Kenney CC0 models, required textures, and original license files are stored under apps/client/public/assets/kenney.
docs/assets.md records pack versions, sources, project use, and modifications.
The glTF 2 loader and required unlit-material extension load on demand; the production PWA build succeeds and a browser playtest verifies all assets load from the Pages base path.

tasks.title: Add drivable offline training vehicles
acceptanceCriteria: The player can enter a nearby vehicle, drive it with touch or keyboard movement, and exit it.
Driving preserves camera tracking, map boundaries, collisions, and bot targeting.
Death and scene teardown safely clear the active vehicle state.
evidence: VehicleController and LocalPlayerController implement proximity interaction, enter, drive, exit, collision, boundary, death, and disposal behavior.
Desktop Chromium verifies entering with E, driving, synchronized player position, and exiting on 2026-09-20.

tasks.title: Configure Firebase guest and Google authentication
acceptanceCriteria: Guests receive anonymous identities.
Anonymous identities can link to Google without silently losing progress.
The server verifies Firebase ID tokens.
evidence: Client entry screen supports Firebase anonymous sign-in, Google sign-in, anonymous-to-Google linking, explicit account-conflict confirmation, sign-out, and persistent local sessions.

GitHub Pages build receives Firebase public web configuration from the github-pages environment; Playwright verifies login-first startup, portrait entry, explicit offline training, and return-to-menu behavior.

tasks.title: Implement the authenticated WebSocket handshake
acceptanceCriteria: Tokens are sent in an application handshake rather than a URL.
The server validates origin, token, protocol version, message size, and rate.
Failures return explicit protocol errors without exposing internals.

tasks.title: Implement server-authoritative movement
acceptanceCriteria: Clients send sequenced inputs rather than transforms.
The server validates and simulates movement at a fixed 20 Hz.
Impossible magnitudes, rates, timestamps, and sequence jumps are rejected.

tasks.title: Implement client prediction and reconciliation
acceptanceCriteria: The local player predicts unacknowledged input.
Authoritative acknowledgements reconcile without persistent drift.
Teleports and respawns bypass normal smoothing.

tasks.title: Implement remote-player snapshot interpolation
acceptanceCriteria: Remote entities render from a bounded interpolation buffer.
Late or missing snapshots do not produce invalid transforms.

tasks.title: Implement server-authoritative pistol combat
acceptanceCriteria: The server validates fire cadence, state, ammo, reload, range, and aim plausibility.
Clients receive authoritative shot, damage, elimination, and respawn events.
Clients cannot declare hits or rewards.

tasks.title: Implement capped lag compensation
acceptanceCriteria: The server keeps a bounded transform history and rewinds eligible target hitboxes.
Claims older than the configured maximum are rejected or clamped.
Latency compensation tests cover current, delayed, and abusive shot times.

tasks.title: Implement authoritative online Team Deathmatch
acceptanceCriteria: The server owns teams, countdown, timer, score, result, reset, and spawn selection.
A player leaving cannot crash or permanently block the room.

tasks.title: Implement disconnect and reconnect handling
acceptanceCriteria: Transient disconnects retry with capped exponential backoff for up to 15 seconds.
A reconnect requires the same user and a valid reconnect token.
Failure returns to the menu with a clear reason.

tasks.title: Verify the two-player multiplayer gate
acceptanceCriteria: Two real mobile devices complete three consecutive matches.
Movement, shots, health, eliminations, score, timer, disconnect, and reconnect are verified.
Results and discovered limits are recorded.

tasks.title: Implement Quick Play room filling and join-in-progress
acceptanceCriteria: Quick Play fills an eligible open room while maintaining balanced teams.
Late joiners receive the current authoritative state and a safe spawn.
A match starts only when both teams have a player.

tasks.title: Implement Firestore player profiles
acceptanceCriteria: Profiles store the minimum schema defined in the GDD.
Only the backend can modify authoritative progression fields.
Schema versions and timestamps are recorded.

tasks.title: Implement levels and XP rewards
acceptanceCriteria: The server awards configured completion, win, and elimination XP.
Level progression is bounded from 1 through 100.
Retries cannot award the same match twice.

tasks.title: Implement Power Point rewards
acceptanceCriteria: The server awards configured completion and win currency.
Transactions use unique IDs and are idempotent.
Clients cannot directly modify balances.

tasks.title: Implement menu, profile, and result flows
acceptanceCriteria: Players can enter Quick Play, inspect level and Power Points, view results, replay, and return to menu.
Unavailable future features are not presented as functional.

tasks.title: Add privacy-minimal observability
acceptanceCriteria: Metrics cover connections, rooms, tick duration, snapshot traffic, errors, matches, and reconnect outcomes.
Client errors exclude free-form personal content.
Production logs exclude successful per-tick traffic.

tasks.title: Create headless multiplayer load clients
acceptanceCriteria: Headless clients authenticate in a test environment, join rooms, move, aim, fire, and remain connected.
Runs are bounded by client count and duration.
Results report errors, latency, traffic, and completion.

tasks.title: Verify the four-player public-test gate
acceptanceCriteria: Four players complete three consecutive matches without restart, unrecoverable desync, or client crash.
The installed PWA reaches the secure production WebSocket endpoint.
Performance, cost, and operational evidence meet the GDD success criteria.

tasks.title: Profile simulation and network capacity
acceptanceCriteria: CPU, memory, tick percentiles, bandwidth, errors, and cost per player-hour are recorded.
The largest stable room size is identified without changing the advertised cap.

tasks.title: Run stepped load tests from 4 to 20 players
acceptanceCriteria: Bounded tests run at 4, 8, 12, 16, and 20 clients.
Each approved step meets server tick, traffic, error, and reconciliation budgets.
A real-device match verifies each approved capacity step.

tasks.title: Decide the multi-instance room ownership strategy
acceptanceCriteria: The decision compares one larger instance, instance-aware routing, and a dedicated game-server platform.
The design does not rely on best-effort session affinity as a room ownership guarantee.
The choice includes expected baseline and player-hour cost.

tasks.title: Publish the verified player cap
acceptanceCriteria: Configuration, UI, and documentation use the highest verified capacity and no higher value.
If 20 players are not verified, the lower supported cap remains explicit.

tasks.title: Implement the extensible character catalog
acceptanceCriteria: Character definitions, selection, ownership, and persistence support adding content without core-code changes.
One original character remains fully usable.

tasks.title: Implement cosmetic costumes and unlocks
acceptanceCriteria: Cosmetics alter presentation only.
Unlock requirements and Power Point spending are server-authoritative and idempotent.
Asset license metadata is recorded.

tasks.title: Implement one simple vehicle
acceptanceCriteria: The vehicle has server-authoritative entry, exit, movement, collision, and replication.
Vehicle use preserves mobile performance and cannot bypass map boundaries.

tasks.title: Add isolated additional game modes
acceptanceCriteria: Each new mode implements the documented GameMode contract.
Core networking does not accumulate mode-specific conditionals.
Each mode has independent rule and lifecycle tests.

tasks.title: Implement the optional AI costume idea service
acceptanceCriteria: The feature is separately deployable and guarded by a feature flag.
Its failure cannot block login, matchmaking, progression, or normal costume selection.
Moderation, rate limits, originality safeguards, and a separate cost budget are verified before enablement.

tasks.title: Fix playtest defects: visible enemy fire, mouse aim, vehicle driving, weapon scale
acceptanceCriteria: Bot attacks render a visible tracer, muzzle flash, impact marker, and a visible bot weapon.
Mouse aim uses canvas CSS pixels and is recomputed every frame so it revolves around the moving player.
Vehicles keep driving instead of colliding with the driver's own collider, and steer smoothly.
The player's pistol is scaled to the character model instead of being oversized.
evidence: ShotEffects renders pooled tracer, muzzle flash, and impact meshes; TrainingBotController gives each bot a weapon and spawns an effect on every attack.
DesktopAimController now passes CSS-pixel pointer coordinates to createPickingRay (fixing the device-pixel-ratio double scaling) and refreshes aim on every frame.
LocalPlayerController disables the player collider while driving and lerps vehicle heading at 3.4 rad/s.
PistolController geometry and offsets reduced ~2.5x to match the 2.25 unit tall character.
npm run validate and 8/8 Playwright tests pass; desktop tests now assert >6 units of sustained vehicle travel, opposing aim vectors across the player, and non-zero bot shot effects on 2026-09-20.
Screenshot playtest confirms a visible red enemy beam hitting the driven car and a correctly sized pistol.

tasks.title: Make bots fair and run offline training as a round match
acceptanceCriteria: Bots have a limited engagement range and distance-based accuracy instead of guaranteed hits at any reach.
Bots need a reaction delay with unobstructed line of sight before firing, and missed shots are visibly rendered.
Offline training runs as a best-of-five round match with a frozen warmup, no mid-round respawns, and a full reset every round.
Eliminated combatants stay out until the next round, so no side can be farmed at its spawn point.
evidence: New game-config bots block: 11 m engagement range, 60 percent accuracy at 4 m falling to 15 percent at maximum range, 20 point moving-target penalty, 500 ms reaction time, three-shot bursts with 1.8 s recovery, and 8 HP per hit.
New simulation modules RoundMatch and computeBotHitChance carry the rules, covered by 15 unit tests (27 simulation tests pass).
OfflineCombatController drives warmup, in_progress, round_ended, intermission, and match_ended phases and resets every combatant at round start instead of respawning mid-round.
TrainingBotController holds fire outside a live round, requires line of sight for the full reaction time, rolls per-shot accuracy, and renders deflected tracers for misses.
10/10 Playwright tests pass, including new cases for the frozen warmup and for bots missing shots.
150 s playtest on 2026-09-20 recorded rounds 1-3 cycling warmup to in_progress to round_ended to intermission to match_ended, with 40 of 83 bot shots hitting a stationary player.
